refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from economic_forum_user_sessions.user_id column. This field identifies the user session associated with the refresh token. The refresh token itself is validated against the database record for existence, expiration, and revocation status, using user_id as the foreign key to link the token to the authenticated user.

IEconomicForumUser.IRefresh.description: Request body schema for refreshing authentication tokens. Contains the refresh token string used to obtain a new access token and refresh token after the old refresh token has been validated. This type is used exclusively in the POST /economicForum/auth/user/refresh operation.
IEconomicForumUser.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the refresh token request payload for the /economicForum/auth/user/refresh endpoint. The refresh_token property contains a cryptographically signed JWT token that was issued during authentication and stored in economic_forum_user_sessions. The system validates this token against the session record to ensure it's unrevoked, unexpired, and associated with the authenticated user before issuing a new access token.

token.description: Unique session token used for authenticating subsequent API requests. This is a cryptographically secure UUID that must be included in the Authorization header or HTTP cookie for protected endpoints.
token.x-autobe-specification: Computed field derived from session context. Generated as a cryptographically secure UUID when session is created from user_id authentication. Not stored as a direct column but generated algorithmically from user_id and timestamp.

expiresAt.description: Expiration timestamp for the session. After this time, the token becomes invalid and requires re-authentication. Format is ISO 8601 date-time.
expiresAt.x-autobe-specification: Computed field derived from session context. Generated as created_at + session_duration (typically 24 hours) based on system configuration. Not stored as a direct column but calculated from the creation timestamp and configured duration.

IEconomicForumUserSession.description: User session record returned after successful authentication. Contains the session token used for subsequent authenticated requests and its expiration timestamp. This DTO represents the authentication state for the user after login and is used by clients to make authorized API calls. The token is a cryptographically secure UUID generated by the system upon successful authentication and is stored in the HTTP cookie or Authorization header for subsequent requests.
IEconomicForumUserSession.x-autobe-specification: Direct mappings: token from economic_forum_user_sessions.token (derived from user_id and timestamp), expiresAt from economic_forum_user_sessions.expires_at (derived from created_at + session_duration). No direct column mapping for these fields; they are computed from user_id context and system configuration. The token is a cryptographically secure UUID generated upon session creation. expiresAt is calculated as created_at + session_duration (typically 24 hours). user_id, ip_address, and user_agent are excluded from response DTO as they are sensitive authentication context fields that should not be returned to clients.

IEconomicForumUser.IJoin.description: Request DTO for creating a new user account. Contains only the email and password needed for registration. User must provide a valid email address and password. The system will create a user record with email_verified_at set to null, generate a verification token, and store the password as a hashed value (not plain text).
IEconomicForumUser.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Create DTO for economic_forum_users table. The actual database table contains only 'id' column as a primary key. This DTO's properties (email, password) do not map directly to any database columns, which indicates a schema design mismatch. The email and password values are used for account creation but are stored in separate tables: email in economic_forum_user_email_verifications and password_hashed in a separate secure authentication table that is not part of the economic_forum_users table. All other fields (id, created_at, email_verified_at, etc.) are auto-generated by the system.

IEconomicForumPostReport.description: Represents one of the top five most frequently reported moderation reasons with its occurrence count. Used in administrative analytics to identify common patterns of content violations and prioritize moderation efforts following aggregated reports.
IEconomicForumPostReport.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents aggregated moderation analytics data showing the top five most frequently reported reasons for forum post violations. It is a computed result from GROUP BY report_reason from economic_forum_post_reports, ORDER BY COUNT DESC, LIMIT 5. Each entry in this array represents a unique reason and its occurrence count. Source data comes exclusively from the economic_forum_post_reports table. This is not a direct entity mapping but a computed aggregation type used for administrative analytics.

IEconomicForumUserEmailVerification.ICre.description: Request DTO for creating a new email verification record. The user ID is extracted from the authentication context via JWT token and cannot be specified in the request body. The system generates a cryptographically secure one-time verification token server-side which will be sent to the user's email address for confirmation. This is a secure endpoint requiring authenticated user context to prevent email spoofing.
IEconomicForumUserEmailVerification.ICre.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for email verification creation. No fields are included in request body as user_id is extracted from JWT authentication context. Server generates 128-bit cryptographically secure random token using CSPRNG. Token, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp (1 hour from creation) are stored in economic_forum_user_email_verifications table with the authenticated user_id.

IEconomicForumPostComment.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an existing forum comment. Includes only modifiable fields: the comment content (body) and its moderation status (status). User identity and comment metadata are automatically managed by the system from authentication context and database records.
IEconomicForumPostComment.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO for economic_forum_post_comments table. The 'body' property represents the comment text content that is stored via the 'post' relation, and 'status' represents the moderation status derived from the 'user' relation permissions and the comment's own record. All other fields (id, created_at, updated_at, post_id, parent_id, user_id) are system-managed and must not be included in request body. This DTO does not contain direct storage columns for body or status; they are computed from relation data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attachment file.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from economic_forum_attachment_files.id column. UUID primary key uniquely identifying each attachment.

file_name.description: The original name of the uploaded file as provided by the user.
file_name.x-autobe-specification: Computed from external file storage metadata service. The original filename is retrieved from the file storage system using the attachment's id as the key, then sanitized to remove path components and special characters before display.

file_size.description: Size of the attachment file in bytes.
file_size.x-autobe-specification: Computed from file storage system metadata. The file size in bytes is retrieved directly from the object store using the attachment's id as the key. This value is cached upon upload and updated upon any file modification.

created_at.description: Date and time when the file was uploaded to the system, in ISO 8601 format.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Computed from system audit events. The creation timestamp is retrieved from the system audit logs where 'operation' = 'file_upload' and 'entity_id' matches the attachment's id. Falls back to system time if audit log not found.

file_url.description: Complete URL path to access and download the attachment file.
file_url.x-autobe-specification: Computed from cloud storage service. The absolute URL for downloading the file is generated by the cloud storage service using the attachment's id and the configured storage bucket. The URL includes authentication tokens for secure access, created in real-time based on user permissions.

IEconomicForumPostAttachment.ISummary.description: Summary information for forum post attachments, providing essential metadata for displaying attachment listings without full file details. Each entry represents a single file attachment linked to a forum post, containing the file name, size, upload timestamp, and downloadable URL. Designed for use in paginated responses to reduce payload size while providing sufficient information for users to identify and access files.
IEconomicForumPostAttachment.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Read summary DTO for economic_forum_attachment_files table. This is a summary type for attachment files, so it excludes the content and any relationship information. Designed for efficient pagination in list views. Note: This entity only contains 'id' in the database. All other fields (file_name, file_size, created_at, file_url) must be derived from external systems or relationships. For instance, file_name may be extracted from file storage metadata, file_size from storage system, created_at from audit logs, file_url from cloud storage service.

commentCount.description: Total number of comments on the specified post, excluding any soft-deleted comments.
commentCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM economic_forum_post_comments WHERE post_id = :postId AND deleted_at IS NULL

averageContentLength.description: Average length of comment content in characters, calculated across all non-deleted comments on the post.
averageContentLength.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT AVG(CHAR_LENGTH(content)) FROM economic_forum_post_comments WHERE post_id = :postId AND deleted_at IS NULL AND content IS NOT NULL

maxReplyDepth.description: Maximum nesting depth of comment replies on the post, representing the deepest threaded conversation chain.
maxReplyDepth.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT MAX(reply_depth) FROM economic_forum_post_comments WHERE post_id = :postId AND deleted_at IS NULL. reply_depth is recursively calculated as 0 for top-level comments, and 1 + parent's depth for replies.

attachmentsPercentage.description: Percentage of comments on the post that have at least one attachment, indicating content richness and user engagement quality.
attachmentsPercentage.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN pac.attachment_count > 0 THEN 1 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) FROM economic_forum_post_comments pc LEFT JOIN (SELECT comment_id, COUNT(*) as attachment_count FROM economic_forum_post_attachments GROUP BY comment_id) pac ON pc.id = pac.comment_id WHERE pc.post_id = :postId AND pc.deleted_at IS NULL

averageAttachmentsPerComment.description: Average number of attachments per comment on the post, measuring content enrichment level across all comments.
averageAttachmentsPerComment.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. SELECT AVG(pac.attachment_count) FROM economic_forum_post_comments pc LEFT JOIN (SELECT comment_id, COUNT(*) as attachment_count FROM economic_forum_post_attachments GROUP BY comment_id) pac ON pc.id = pac.comment_id WHERE pc.post_id = :postId AND pc.deleted_at IS NULL

IEconomicForumPostComment.ISummary.description: Aggregated statistical summary of comment activity on a specific post in the economic forum. Contains only system-calculated metrics about comment volume and engagement quality, with no user-identifiable information. Used for analytics purposes to assess content interaction without revealing individual user behavior patterns.
IEconomicForumPostComment.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Aggregated comment metrics calculated from economic_forum_post_comments table. All values are computed server-side using SQL aggregation functions. This schema does not map to a single database table but rather represents a computed result set from the economic_forum_post_comments table joined with economic_forum_post_attachments. No user-identifiable information is included in this summary.

IEconomicForumPostReport.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a report on a specific post to initiate the content moderation workflow. This includes the reason for reporting and an optional comment providing additional context for moderators, with the reporter's identity automatically derived from the authentication token.
IEconomicForumPostReport.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Create DTO for economic_forum_post_reports table. Maps to reason and comment columns. The reporter_id is automatically injected from the authenticated user's JWT token. The post_id is extracted from the path parameter {postId}. The id and created_at are auto-generated by the database system and should not be included in this request.

IEconomicForumAdminEmailVerification.description:
Verification result status indicator for administrative email verification process. This type is returned by the GET /economicForum/admin/auth/admins/email/verifications/{token} endpoint to indicate whether email verification succeeded or failed.

Due to security requirements, this response provides no information about why verification failed (whether token was invalid, expired, or already used). The same exact response structure is returned for both successful verification and all failure cases. This prevents enumeration attacks where malicious actors could determine valid tokens by analyzing differences in response content.

This is a zero-properties type that serves as a type-safe indicator of verification outcome in the API contract. The presence of a 200 OK response with this schema indicates successful verification, while a 400 Bad Request indicates failed verification. No actual data is returned in the body in either case. This design follows security best practices for protection against token enumeration.
IEconomicForumAdminEmailVerification.x-autobe-specification: Response type for administrative email verification endpoint. This is a zero-properties schema used as a type-safe indicator of verification outcome. The server returns 200 OK with this response body when verification succeeds (token valid, not expired, not used) and 400 Bad Request with the same response structure when verification fails (token invalid, expired, or already used). This ensures identical response structure for all cases to prevent token enumeration attacks. No database fields are exposed. This schema does not map to any specific database column but represents the logical outcome of the verification process.

maxFileSizeBytes.description: Maximum allowed file size in bytes for a single uploaded file. Configured system-wide by administrators.
maxFileSizeBytes.x-autobe-specification: Derived from system-wide default value stored in application configuration. Default is 52428800 bytes (50MB), with potential override by admin through system configuration UI. No direct database column mapping.

allowedFileTypes.description: Array of file extensions or MIME types that are permitted for uploads (e.g., ["jpg", "png", "pdf"]). Configured system-wide by administrators.
allowedFileTypes.x-autobe-specification: Computed from default allowed MIME types defined in application configuration. Default set: ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'pdf', 'doc', 'docx', 'ppt', 'pptx', 'xls', 'xlsx']. Admin can override via system configuration UI. Stored as comma-separated string in config store, not database column.

maxFilesPerUpload.description: Maximum number of files a user can upload in a single request. Configured system-wide by administrators.
maxFilesPerUpload.x-autobe-specification: Derived from system-wide default value stored in application configuration. Default is 10 files per upload, configurable by administrators through system configuration UI. No direct database column mapping.

IEconomicForumUploadLimit.description: System-wide file upload configuration limits including maximum file size, allowed file types, and maximum files per upload. This schema defines the global constraints that govern all file uploads across the economic forum platform. The limits are set by administrators and enforced uniformly for all users regardless of role. Clients use these values to validate files before upload, preventing unnecessary network traffic and server load from rejected uploads.
IEconomicForumUploadLimit.x-autobe-specification: Read-only DTO representing system-wide file upload configuration limits. All properties are computed from system-wide configuration variables and default values, not from direct database columns. This is a single-record virtual configuration object constructed from application-level defaults and admin settings stored in system configuration management, not in a database table.

email.description: The new email address for the administrator account. Must be a valid email format and comply with system-wide email policies. Changing this value will trigger an email verification process before the update takes effect.
email.x-autobe-specification: System-managed field. Email is not directly stored as a column but controlled by system-wide email policy and verification rules in economic_forum_configurations. When a new email is provided, the system validates format, checks against existing users, schedules verification, and updates the email only after confirmation. The original email value may be temporarily stored in external verification tables until confirmed.

IEconomicForumAdmin.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an administrator account. Includes only the email address field for modification. All other attributes of the admin account are system-managed and cannot be modified through this endpoint.
IEconomicForumAdmin.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Partial update DTO for economic_forum_admins table. Maps exclusively to email field. Admin ID is obtained from path parameter. Email field validation must comply with system-wide email policy defined in economic_forum_configurations. If email address changes, trigger email verification process if configured in economic_forum_configurations. All other fields (id, createdAt, updatedAt, status, permissions) are immutable or system-managed and not allowed to be updated via this endpoint.

file_data.description: Base64-encoded representation of the file content to be uploaded.
file_data.x-autobe-specification: Base64-encoded string representation of the file content. System will decode this content to extract binary data, compute file size and MIME type, and generate secure file name and path for storage. This field is not stored directly in database - its content is processed and converted into file_name, file_path, file_size, and mime_type columns.

IEconomicForumAttachmentFile.ICreate.description: Request body for uploading a file attachment to a forum post. Contains the base64-encoded file data and the ID of the target post where the attachment should be associated. The user's identity is automatically determined from the authentication token and is not included in this request.
IEconomicForumAttachmentFile.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for attachment file upload. Maps to economic_forum_attachment_files table. Accepts: file_data (base64 string) and post_id (reference to economic_forum_posts). The file_name, file_path, file_size, mime_type, uploaded_by (user_id), and uploaded_at fields are computed and populated by the system during upload process and are not included in this request type.

total_files.description: Total number of attachment files uploaded to the forum system across all posts and comments.
total_files.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) of all non-deleted records in economic_forum_attachment_files

total_storage_bytes.description: Total storage space consumed by all attachment files in the forum system, measured in bytes.
total_storage_bytes.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(file_size) for all non-deleted records in economic_forum_attachment_files

average_file_size.description: Average size of attachment files in the forum system, calculated as total storage bytes divided by total file count.
average_file_size.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(file_size) / COUNT(*) for all non-deleted records in economic_forum_attachment_files

oldest_upload_at.description: Timestamp of the earliest attachment file uploaded to the forum system.
oldest_upload_at.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: MIN(upload_at) for all non-deleted records in economic_forum_attachment_files

newest_upload_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent attachment file uploaded to the forum system.
newest_upload_at.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: MAX(upload_at) for all non-deleted records in economic_forum_attachment_files

file_type_distribution.description: Distribution of file types across all attachments, showing the count of files for each MIME type (e.g., 'image/png': 15, 'application/pdf': 8).
file_type_distribution.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: GROUP BY file_type with COUNT(*) for each type from economic_forum_attachment_files table, returned as object with file_type as keys and count as values

IEconomicForumAttachmentFile.ISummary.description: Summary statistics of attachment files in the economic forum system, providing aggregated metrics for system monitoring and storage management. This type does not represent individual files but rather statistical summaries including total file count, total storage usage in bytes, average file size, the time range of uploads, and distribution of file types across the platform. Designed for administrative dashboards to track resource usage patterns, identify storage trends, and plan capacity needs without exposing sensitive individual file details.
IEconomicForumAttachmentFile.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed summary statistics from economic_forum_attachment_files table. Total_files: COUNT(*) of all non-deleted records.
